framework.name: DevOps & CI/CD Security Evaluation
framework.description: Evaluates the deployment pipeline, infrastructure security, monitoring, and operational practices for the FGC platform. Covers GitHub Actions CI/CD, Proxmox homelab deployment, Docker containerization, nginx reverse proxy, Cloudflare Tunnel, and operational monitoring.

context.deployment: GitHub Actions -> Tailscale OAuth -> rsync -> nginx restart
context.services: nginx reverse proxy, PostgreSQL, Redis, Node.js services (bot:4100, attendance:4201)

rubric.1-2: Critical: Pipeline or infrastructure actively compromised or compromisable.
rubric.3-4: Poor: Major security gaps in deployment or infrastructure.
rubric.5-6: Fair: Basic pipeline works but security controls lacking.
rubric.7-8: Good: Solid pipeline with proper secret handling and some monitoring.
rubric.9-10: Excellent: Defense in depth from code commit to production with full observability.

criteria.name: GitHub Actions Security
what_to_check: Workflow files (.github/workflows/) don't contain hardcoded secrets
All secrets use GitHub Secrets (${{ secrets.NAME }}), not environment variables in YAML
Actions are pinned to specific SHA or version (not @latest or @main)
Third-party actions are from trusted sources and audited
Workflow permissions are minimal (not permissions: write-all)
Pull request workflows from forks can't access secrets
Branch protection rules enforce review before merge to main
criteria.remediation: Pin all actions to SHA. Set minimal permissions per workflow. Review all third-party actions. Ensure branch protection requires review.

criteria.name: Secret Management in CI
what_to_check: CODEANT_TOKEN (if used), Tailscale keys, SSH keys are in GitHub Secrets
Secrets are not echoed in logs (no 'echo $SECRET' in scripts)
Deployment SSH keys are scoped (not root access)
Tailscale OAuth token has minimal permissions
Secrets are rotated periodically
criteria.remediation: Audit all workflow files for secret handling. Use GitHub Actions masks for any dynamic secret values. Scope SSH keys to deployment user only.

criteria.name: Build & Deploy Process
what_to_check: Build artifacts are verified before deployment (checksums, tests pass)
Deploy only happens on main branch (not on PRs or feature branches)
Rollback mechanism exists (can quickly revert to previous version)
Build environment is clean (no persistent state between builds)
npm ci used instead of npm install (deterministic installs)
criteria.remediation: Add build verification step. Implement rollback script. Use npm ci for reproducible builds.

criteria.name: Automated Security Checks in Pipeline
what_to_check: npm audit runs in CI (fails on high/critical vulnerabilities)
Linting runs in CI (ESLint with security rules)
Dependency check runs before deploy
Optional: SAST scanning (CodeAnt.ai, Semgrep, or similar)
Build fails on security violations (not just warnings)
criteria.remediation: Add npm audit --audit-level=high to CI. Add ESLint with eslint-plugin-security. Consider free SAST tools.

criteria.name: Environment Parity Check
what_to_check: scripts/check-env-parity.mjs exists and runs in CI pipeline
Validates env vars across all .env.example files (bot, attendance, website)
Catches drift between services (missing vars, typos, stale entries)
Fails the build if parity check fails
Coverage: does it check all services or only some?
known_issues: scripts/check-env-parity.mjs was added as a quality gate — evaluate its coverage and whether it catches real drift
criteria.remediation: Ensure check-env-parity.mjs is in CI pipeline and blocks deploys on failure. Verify it covers all .env.example files across all services.

criteria.name: Proxmox & Server Hardening
what_to_check: SSH access uses key-only auth (password disabled)
SSH port is non-default or protected by Tailscale/VPN
Firewall (ufw/iptables) is configured and active
Unnecessary services are disabled
Automatic security updates enabled (unattended-upgrades)
Server is not running services as root
criteria.remediation: Disable SSH password auth. Configure ufw to allow only required ports. Enable unattended-upgrades. Run services as non-root users.

criteria.name: nginx Configuration
what_to_check: nginx is up to date
Server tokens are hidden (server_tokens off)
HTTPS is enforced (redirect HTTP -> HTTPS)
Security headers added in nginx config (if not handled by app)
Rate limiting at nginx level for additional protection
Access to admin paths is IP-restricted or behind additional auth
Proxy headers are set correctly (X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Forwarded-Proto)
criteria.remediation: Add server_tokens off. Configure security headers. Set correct proxy headers for Express to see real IPs.

criteria.name: Cloudflare Tunnel Security
what_to_check: Tunnel token is stored securely (not in source code)
Access policies are configured in Cloudflare dashboard
Only intended services are exposed through the tunnel
Cloudflare WAF rules are enabled (even basic free tier)
Bot protection is enabled
criteria.remediation: Review Cloudflare Tunnel configuration. Ensure only intended routes are exposed. Enable available WAF protections.

criteria.name: Database & Redis Security
what_to_check: PostgreSQL is not exposed to the internet (localhost or private network only)
PostgreSQL uses password auth (not trust) for all connections
Redis is bound to localhost or requires a password
Database backups are automated and tested
PostgreSQL user has minimal privileges (not superuser for app connections)
PostgreSQL pool is configured with max:20, min:2, idleTimeoutMillis:30000, connectionTimeoutMillis:5000 — verify these values are appropriate for expected load
criteria.remediation: Verify pg_hba.conf restricts to localhost. Set Redis bind to 127.0.0.1 with requirepass. Create app-specific DB user with limited grants.

criteria.name: Dockerfile Best Practices
what_to_check: Base images are pinned to specific versions (not :latest)
Multi-stage builds used to minimize final image size
Running as non-root user in container
No secrets in Docker build args or layers
.dockerignore excludes sensitive files (.env, .git, node_modules)
HEALTHCHECK defined for service containers
criteria.remediation: Pin base images. Add USER directive. Create .dockerignore. Add HEALTHCHECK.

criteria.name: Docker Compose Configuration
what_to_check: Services use restart policies (restart: unless-stopped)
Ports are bound to localhost where not needed externally
Environment variables use env_file, not hardcoded in compose
Volume mounts are minimal (only what's needed)
Network segmentation: frontend, backend, database on separate networks
pg-backup service is configured — verify volume mount for backups, restart policy, and that DATABASE_URL isn't hardcoded in docker-compose.yml
criteria.remediation: Use Docker networks for segmentation. Bind internal services to 127.0.0.1. Use env_file for all secrets.

criteria.name: Application Logging
what_to_check: Structured logging format (JSON) for easy parsing
Log levels used appropriately (error, warn, info, debug)
Request logging with correlation IDs
Logs are persisted (not just stdout that disappears on restart)
Log rotation configured (logs don't fill disk)
Phase 5 added request logging to the website API (method, path, status, duration) — verify it doesn't log request bodies (PII risk) and skips health check endpoints
known_issues: Bot service has structured JSON logging and monitoring route with dependency health probes
Main website API only got basic request logging in Phase 5 — note the gap in logging maturity between services
criteria.remediation: Use winston or pino for structured logging. Configure log rotation. Add request correlation IDs.

criteria.name: Health Checks & Uptime
what_to_check: Health check endpoints exist for each service (/health or /healthz)
Health checks verify downstream dependencies (DB, Redis)
Process manager (PM2, systemd, Docker) restarts crashed services
Uptime monitoring is configured (UptimeRobot, Healthchecks.io, or similar)
Alerting on service downtime (email, WhatsApp notification to admin)
criteria.remediation: Add /health endpoints. Configure PM2 or Docker restart policies. Set up free UptimeRobot monitoring.

criteria.name: Error Tracking
what_to_check: Unhandled exceptions are captured and reported
Frontend errors are tracked (Sentry free tier or similar)
Backend errors are logged with full stack traces (server-side only)
WhatsApp bot errors are tracked (failed message sends, webhook errors)
BullMQ failed jobs are monitored
criteria.remediation: Consider Sentry free tier for error tracking. Monitor BullMQ dead letter queue. Set up alerts for repeated errors.

criteria.name: Database Backups
what_to_check: scripts/pg-backup.sh exists and Docker pg-backup service is configured — verify they actually run, produce valid backups, and rotation works (keep 7 days)
Backups are stored off-server (or at minimum, separate drive)
Backup restoration has been tested (at least once)
Backup retention policy is enforced (automated cleanup of old backups)
Backups are encrypted if stored remotely
known_issues: scripts/pg-backup.sh and Docker pg-backup service were added — verify they produce valid, restorable backups
criteria.remediation: Test backup restoration: run pg_restore on a recent backup to verify integrity. Verify retention rotation. Consider off-site backup storage. Document recovery steps.

criteria.name: Configuration Backups
what_to_check: nginx configs, Docker configs, .env templates are version controlled
Server setup is documented (can be recreated from documentation)
Cloudflare Tunnel configuration is documented
DNS records are documented
criteria.remediation: Create infrastructure-as-code documentation. Version control all config files (without secrets). Document server setup steps.

evaluation_instructions.for_claude_code: Evaluate by: 1) Review .github/workflows/ files for CI/CD patterns, 2) Check Dockerfiles and docker-compose.yml, 3) Review nginx configuration files, 4) Check for health endpoints in Express apps, 5) Review logging configuration, 6) Check for backup scripts/cron jobs. Note: Some infrastructure items (server config, Cloudflare settings) may need manual verification — flag these as 'requires manual check' with instructions for what to verify.
